title: review: tool disclosure active (T-0918), focused security-path review (retry)
spec: Security-path review of branch task/T-0918 in worktree /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator/wt/T-0918 against goal/T-0760 (11 files). Post a verdict within 25 turns: approve, or request_changes with file:line comments. You must call bus_post_result on THIS task id only; do not read or write any other task in the bus. Focus in this order and stop when done: (1) spawn.run_worker active branch: the minimal allowlist never drops mandatory tools (Read, bus_post_result, git for review/scout, Edit/Write/tests-green for execute), and shadow/off launches are byte-identical to before; (2) the one-shot escalation: _hidden_tool_request reads result.reason with the NEEDS_TOOL_PREFIX constant, the second run uses the full legacy allowlist, budget/timeout come from the remainder, no third run, usage of both runs released once; (3) tool_escalation_used stamp and hidden_tool_recovery_rate in context_scorecard.by_role_task_class; (4) prompt files only add the one escalation sentence. Run tests/test_spawn.py and tests/test_tool_catalog.py inside the worktree. Do not re-derive the design; do not read unrelated files. Return ONLY the required JSON verdict via bus_post_result, with no other bus writes.
acceptance: verdict approve or request_changes with file:line comments

comments.issue: The one-respawn-per-task cap is only enforced within a single run_worker() call (it's a plain if/else, not a loop). It is not enforced across separate invocations: nothing checks t.get('pipeline',{}).get('tool_escalation_used') before allowing escalation. If a held task (e.g. the 'no budget for respawn' skip path, or any other reason) is later resumed and run_worker(task_id) is called again, and the worker again posts a needs_tool hold, the code will escalate a second time, granting the full legacy allowlist and burning a fresh budget reservation. This contradicts the spec text repeated in both v1 ('respawn capped at one per task') and v2 ('the second attempt logs tool_escalation_used ... respawn capped at one per task'). No acceptance test covers the cross-invocation case since all three spawn tests exercise a single run_worker() call, so the gate does not catch this.
